business.title: Intelligent monitoring of human behaviour in dementia care: a non-contact multimodal AIoT approach in real-world elderly support
business.description: Dementia is a progressive neurodegenerative condition that unfolds at different rates across individuals and presents major challenges for elderly care. Fluctuating cognitive functions and the occurrence of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD) reduce patients’ quality of life (QOL) and increase caregiver burden. Continuous and context-aware monitoring is essential to support early detection and effective care strategies. This study developed a multimodal, non-contact monitoring framework that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensors to continuously capture behavioural patterns such as gait and sleep. A quantification model was constructed to estimate cognitive function in alignment with Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores. Furthermore, a predictive framework for BPSD onset was developed by combining behavioural, sleep, and environmental data. Machine learning models were trained and validated using multi-facility data collected over two years. The quantification model demonstrated particular sensitivity to memory-related domains such as registration and recall, suggesting that subtle behavioural and sleep-related features can serve as practical indicators of cognitive decline. The BPSD prediction model identified environmental and sleep-related factors, particularly temperature, sound, and sleep rhythm, as dominant predictors. Early warnings generated by the system enabled timely caregiver intervention, reducing workload and improving patient well-being. This study presents a comprehensive “non-contact multimodal AI” approach for continuous, objective dementia monitoring. By integrating behavioural, sleep, and environmental signals, the framework enhances early detection of cognitive decline and supports proactive prevention of BPSD. These findings illustrate the potential of AI-driven sensing systems to strengthen dementia-friendly care practices and inform scalable digital health strategies.

business.title: A hybrid AI-blockchain architecture for intelligent zero-trust authentication for large-scale internet of things
business.description: The IoT (Internet of Things) is expanding at a fast pace and one of the biggest security issues is device authentication. Centralized authentication systems have a single point of failure, are not tamper-proof, have no audit trail and unable to detect compromised devices after legitimate registration. In this paper, an authentication framework for IoT that integrates Ethereum’s smart contracts with an XGBoost behavioral classifier is proposed. It is managed through 3 smart contracts, each modular, such as Device Registry, Authentication and Audit that record all authentication events on-chain. Each request for authentication is also created with a challenge from the server, which is signed with the device’s secp256k1 private key, and is just for that request. So that the server can check whether the device has the private key for the registered key, it can test freshness and feature integrity before any inference is performed. The XGBoost model is trained using N-BaIoT traffic from nine physical IoT devices infected by the Mirai and BASHLITE botnets, with Gaussian feature perturbation (α = 1.6) only applied to the training split and 13% label flipping, and scaling, feature selection and hyperparameter selection all fitted on the training split only. The model has a test accuracy of 93.27% and an AUC-ROC of 0.9770 when tested on a clean held-out set. According to the authentication convention where accepting an attack sample is a false acceptance, the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) is 2.67% and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) is 20.27%. A semi-formal BAN logic analysis extracts device key binding, entity authentication and request freshness, server authentication and device-signed non-repudiation, depending on the explicit assumptions. Behavioral assessment is treated as a probabilistic risk signal outside the BAN logic. An adaptive trust scoring controlled ablation demonstrates that the number of requests that the attacker gets approved against a persistently compromised device drops to 0.11 per 1,000 requests, while occasionally hard-penalizing benign devices depends on the penalty setting. The differences in accuracy from the six baselines (Random Forest, SVM, Autoencoder, LightGBM, a multilayer perceptron and Isolation Forest) are statistically significant (Paired t-tests, P < 0.05) and 5-fold stratified cross validation resulted in an accuracy of 93.27% ± 0.20%. With a local Ganache network, an authentication cycle takes 210,408 gas (USD 8.42 at 20 Gwei and ETH = USD 2,000), end-to-end latency of 35.61 ms and 125.8 authentications per second with 20 concurrent devices. A set of 20 device identities (nine physical N-BaIoT devices and eleven synthetic variants that are leveraged just for load generation) are used in system-level experiments. The findings reveal (1) how the design can be implemented on permissioned blockchains (where the transaction fee is zero), and (2) the cost and usage compromises it must accept.

science.title: Insights into collapsibility and structural behaviors of unsaturated loess from a novel discrete element model
science.description: The existing microscopic contact model based on capillary force can effectively simulate the consolidation and collapsibility behaviors of unsaturated loess under low saturation (≤ 30%), yet it fails to characterize the mechanical responses of loess under high saturation conditions and neglects inter-particle chemical bonding. Therefore, an improved microscopic contact model is proposed considering capillary force for full-range saturation conditions, and chemical bonding force by the secondary development and discrete element method (DEM). After the reliability and accuracy are verified through two-particle single-contact model tests, numerical collapse tests are carried out to explore the multi-factor influences of initial water content, relative compaction and chemical bonding strength on the collapsibility deformation of loess. The results demonstrate that the improved model expands the applicable saturation range and can accurately reproduce the wetting-induced collapsibility characteristics of structured loess. The increase of water content accelerates the attenuation of inter-particle capillary force and the softening of chemical bonding strength, which significantly enhances the collapsibility of loess. Higher relative compaction and stronger chemical bonding can effectively inhibit the collapse deformation of loess. Microscopic mechanism analysis reveals that loess collapse is essentially the structural stability loss caused by the weakening of inter-particle connection under hydro-mechanical-chemical coupling effects. These findings can provide a theoretical basis for macro-micro mechanism analysis of unsaturated loess and the prevention of loess collapsibility hazards in geotechnical engineering.
